title: A Deadline for the Border
premise: Cyrus Amberdale, a sleep-wrecked interpreter for a faltering border peace delegation, discovers that a dead linguist's voiceprint — his own voice, cloned — has unlocked a server holding the archive of Amberline, the shadowy language-intelligence network that trained him. As the summit deadline approaches, he realizes the delegation's collapse is being engineered by Amberline to sell its predictive translation system to the highest bidder. Hunted by the network's handlers and betrayed by his mentor, Cyrus chooses truth over loyalty, broadcasting the archive mid-summit and burning Amberline's infrastructure with the cloned voiceprint turned against it. He ends the story sleepless but free, testifying as the border talks finally begin in earnest.
about_author: Wren Yarrow is the pen name of a former field interpreter who spent a decade in delegation rooms across three contested borders before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about the people who carry words between enemies and the institutions that weaponize language.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Insomnia
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Three weeks before the Meridian Pass summit, Cyrus translates a closed-door session and mishears — or refuses to hear — a phrase that mirrors the incident that broke his sleep. That night, an encrypted message arrives: his own voice, recorded years ago, requesting access to a server in Tallinn. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Amberline
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, with a brief interlude from handler Odile Vasse. Cyrus traces the voiceprint request to Amberline, the elite translation institute that recruited him at twenty-two and quietly disappeared from registries in 2019. He contacts his old mentor, Halvard Reyes, who warns him to delete the message. The beat: nostalgia curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Dead Linguist
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. He flies to Tallinn under cover of a delegation logistics trip and finds the requester: Mirela Ost, an Amberline linguist who died nine months ago in an unexplained fall. Her apartment holds a cold-storage drive and a note in cipher: the network never stopped training; it started predicting. Beat: grief for a stranger who knew him.

chapters.title: Predictive Peace
chapters.summary: POV alternating Cyrus and Odile. The drive reveals Amberline's true product: a system that models negotiations and engineers their failure to make its sponsors indispensable. The Meridian summit is its live demonstration. Odile, sensing Cyrus is close, activates his old loyalty contract. Beat: the vertigo of realizing a failure he witnessed was manufactured.

chapters.title: Loyalty Contract
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Halvard arrives in Tallinn, ostensibly to help, and Cyrus must decide whether the man who saved his career is protecting him or herding him. A staged mugging takes the drive's backup; only Mirela's cipher copy survives. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve as Cyrus chooses to trust no one but the dead.

chapters.title: The Summit Convenes
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, embedded with the delegation at Meridian Pass. Talks open badly — too badly, on cue — and Cyrus hears the predictive system's fingerprints in every translated line. He realizes the interpreters' booths are the network's nervous system. Beat: quiet horror in a room built for hope.

chapters.title: What Halvard Knew
chapters.summary: POV Halvard, then Cyrus. Halvard confesses his role: he recruited Cyrus precisely because his voiceprint was clean, unflagged, usable. But he also gives Cyrus the master key — the original voice model — claiming remorse. Cyrus cannot tell if it's a gift or a leash. Beat: betrayal and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus. Using Mirela's cipher and his own cloned voice, Cyrus plans to invert the access: not to open Amberline's servers, but to overwrite them and broadcast the archive to every delegation, journalist, and sponsor on the summit's secure channel. Odile closes in. Beat: cold, focused purpose replacing fear.

chapters.title: Deadline at Meridian
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, real-time. During the summit's final plenary, Cyrus slips into the interpretation chain and triggers the broadcast as Odile's operatives seal the building. Halvard takes a bullet meant for him; the archive floods every screen; the engineered collapse becomes a public scandal mid-session. Beat: the climax — chaos, sacrifice, and a voice turned against its makers.

chapters.title: Sleepless, Free
chapters.summary: POV Cyrus, weeks later. Amberline's sponsors scatter; inquiries begin; the summit reconvenes without the network in the walls. Cyrus testifies, still unable to sleep through the night, but the insomnia no longer feels like guilt — it feels like vigilance. He translates the first honest sentence of the new talks. Beat: bruised, earned resolution.
